title: 95% of Medicare Advantage Denials Get Overturned — When Anyone Appeals
description: A June 2026 HHS Office of Inspector General review of skilled nursing facility admissions found Medicare Advantage organizations overturned 95% of appealed denials — but only 18% of denials were ever appealed in the first place.
sourceCitation: Source: HHS OIG report OEI-09-24-00331, June 2026 (oig.hhs.gov). Educational content only — not legal or financial advice. AI-generated narration.

scenes.captionText: HHS OIG report, June 2026 — 95% of appealed denials overturned.
scenes.narrationText: This comes from a federal watchdog report released in June 2026, looking at skilled nursing facility admissions. When people appealed, 95% of those denials were overturned. But here's the catch: only about one in five people actually appealed.

scenes.captionText: Most people never appeal at all.
scenes.narrationText: Most denials aren't really final. They're a prompt to appeal — and most people never do.

The reason so few people appeal is timing. Most plans give you only a matter of days after a hospital or skilled nursing stay ends to file — the deadline is often noon the day before your coverage ends.

timeline.deadlineLabel: Deadline: noon, day before care ends

scenes.captionText: Ask for your appeal deadline in writing.
scenes.narrationText: If a parent or spouse just had a skilled nursing or rehab stay denied, don't assume it's final. Ask for the appeal deadline in writing today.
